title: Quality Improvement Director
text:
***POSITION PURPOSE:***

The Director of Quality Improvement operates under the leadership and direction of the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) and Chief Operating Officer (COO). The CMO maintains direct clinical oversight of clinical quality improvement activities and regulatory quality programs. The Director of Quality Improvement provides organization-wide leadership for EVCHC's quality improvement program. The Director establishes the quality strategy in partnership with executive, clinical, operational and compliance leaders; converts organizational goals and regulatory requirements into measurable work plans; and leads improvement efforts that strengthen patient outcomes, safety, access, equity and care experience. The Director is accountable for reliable quality data, required clinical quality reporting, continuous improvement methods, Patient Centered Medical Home recognition, and the performance of the Quality Improvement Department.

 

***MAJOR POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES AND FUNCTIONS:***

**Quality Strategy and Governance**

* Lead the development, implementation and annual evaluation of EVCHC's organization-wide Quality Improvement and Quality Assurance Plan in alignment with the strategic plan, clinical standards and applicable Health Center Program requirements.

* Establish annual quality priorities, measures, targets, owners and timelines with executive and clinical leadership. Monitor progress and recommend corrective action when performance does not meet established goals.

* Lead or support the Quality Improvement Committee and related workgroups. Prepare agendas, dashboards, meeting materials, decisions and follow-up reports for executive leadership and the Board of Directors, as requested.

* Advise executive leaders on emerging quality risks, performance trends, resource needs and opportunities to improve care delivery across sites and service lines.

* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, patient safety and learning throughout the organization.

**Department Leadership**

* Direct the work of the Quality Improvement Department, including recruitment, onboarding, supervision, coaching, performance evaluation, workload assignment and staff development.

* Develop departmental goals, staffing plans, procedures and budgets that support timely completion of quality priorities and reporting obligations.

* Set clear expectations for the accuracy, timeliness and usability of analyses, audits, reports and improvement support provided by the department.

* Build effective working relationships with clinical care teams, Operations, Information Technology, Compliance, Human Resources, Finance, Behavioral Health, Dental and other departments involved in quality outcomes.

**Quality Measurement and Reporting**

* Oversee the collection, validation, analysis and submission of clinical quality measures and required reports, including Uniform Data System measures, population health platforms transition and readiness, HEDIS and payer measures, grant measures and internal quality indicators.

* Develop and maintain executive, provider, site and service-line dashboards that show current performance, trends, disparities, targets and improvement actions.

* Track provider and care-team performance, identify variation and care gaps, and provide leaders with actionable information while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data-use standards.

* Establish data-validation controls and documentation so that quality reports can be reconciled to source systems and used as an organization-wide source of truth. Partnering with Director of Data and IT operations for oversight on data governance committee.

* Present quality findings in clear written and verbal reports to the Board, executive leadership, managers, providers, staff, health plans and external reviewers, as appropriate.

**Performance Improvement**

* Lead Plan Do Study Act cycles, root-cause analyses and other structured improvement methods from problem definition through implementation, evaluation and sustainment.

* Partner with clinical and operational leaders to improve preventive care, chronic disease outcomes, access, continuity, patient experience, care coordination, documentation and other priority measures.

* Translate data findings into practical workflow changes, training, decision support, audit tools and accountability processes that can be sustained across sites.

* Evaluate improvement results, identify lessons learned and spread effective practices to other care teams, programs or locations when appropriate **Regulatory Readiness and Patient Safety**

* Lead the quality components of Patient Centered Medical Home recognition and renewal, including evidence collection, workflow assessment, documentation, staff education and sustainment of recognized practices alongside Director of compliance.

* Partner with Compliance Director, Risk Management, clinical leadership and Operations on quality-related readiness for HRSA operational site visits, FTCA deeming and risk-management activities, health plan audits, accreditation reviews and other external assessments.

* Support corrective action plans with the Director of Compliance arising from audits, quality reviews, safety events or regulatory findings. Define measures, monitor completion and verify that corrective actions are effective and sustained.

* Analyze trends in patient safety events, grievances and quality-of-care concerns with the appropriate leaders while protecting confidentiality and following reporting requirements.

* Maintain organized records of quality plans, committee actions, reports, audits, improvement projects and supporting evidence required for oversight and external review.

**Clinical Analytics and Health Information Technology**

* Direct the clinical analytics program and define reporting requirements that support clinical decision-making, population health management and performance improvement.

* Partner with Information Technology and system vendors to improve data extraction, interfaces, registries, care guidelines, clinical decision support, templates and reporting tools used for quality measurement.

* Lead data-governance practices for quality information, including measure definitions, ownership, validation, access, change control and resolution of reporting discrepancies.

* Assess the quality and workflow impact of new digital tools and automation used in clinical or quality processes and recommend safeguards, testing and performance monitoring before broad implementation.

* Recommend redesign of workflows affected by the electronic health record, patient portal, population health platforms and other clinical information systems.

**Organizational Responsibilities**

* Participate in executive, management, clinical and staff meetings related to quality priorities and organizational performance.

* Maintain current knowledge of FQHC quality requirements, clinical quality measures, health plan expectations and recognized improvement practices.

* Protect patient, employee and organizational information and comply with HIPAA, confidentiality, cybersecurity and records-management requirements.

* Perform other job-related duties as assigned within the scope of the position.

***POSITION REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:***

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in public health, health care administration, nursing, health sciences, informatics or a related field is required. A master's degree is preferred.

* At least five years of progressive experience in health care quality improvement, population health, clinical analytics or health care program management is required, including at least three years of supervisory or department leadership experience.

* Experience in a Federally Qualified Health Center, community health center or other safety-net setting is strongly preferred.

* Experience leading cross-functional improvement projects and preparing quality reports for executives, governing boards, health plans or regulatory agencies is required.

* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality, Lean or Six Sigma certification, or comparable quality-improvement training is preferred.

**Knowledge and Skills**

* Working knowledge of continuous quality improvement methods, patient safety practices, clinical quality measurement, health equity and population health management.

* Knowledge of HRSA Health Center Program expectations, Uniform Data System reporting, HEDIS measures, Patient Centered Medical Home standards and payer quality programs is strongly preferred.

* Advanced ability to collect, validate, analyze and present health care data and to translate findings into operational decisions and improvement plans.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint and experience using electronic health records, population health platforms, data visualization tools or clinical reporting applications. Experience with NextGen or comparable systems is preferred.

* Strong leadership, project management, facilitation, written communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build accountability across departments .

* Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet reporting deadlines, exercise sound judgment and communicate sensitive performance information professionally.

* Demonstrated commitment to serving medically underserved communities and reducing disparities in access, care and health outcomes.

***WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL/MENTAL ABILITIES AND PROCESSES:***

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

 

* Work is performed primarily in an office and health center environment and requires regular travel among EVCHC sites and occasional travel to meetings or trainings.

* The position requires extended periods of sitting and computer use, as well as standing, walking, bending, reaching, speaking, hearing and seeing sufficient to perform assigned duties.

* The employee must be able to communicate clearly, review detailed reports, maintain concentration, manage competing deadlines and work effectively in shared office and clinical environments.

* The employee must be able to lift and carry materials and equipment weighing up to 20 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

DOE: $125,000 - $148,824 Annually
